entries.proposition: The design: five point mutations combined from two previously published liver-de-targeted capsids.
entries.snippet: To create the AAV9-DM capsid, we combined the 501, 505, 706, 527, and 533 mutations in one AAV9 capsid (Figure 1A).

entries.proposition: THE COST THE TITLE DOES NOT CARRY: the new capsid packages roughly eight-fold worse than its parent, which works directly against the dose-ceiling argument it is proposed for.
entries.snippet: AAV9 yields were in line with the general field consensus at 3.58 × 1013 vector genomes (vgs) (Figure 1B). We found both AAV9-16 and AAV9-HR to result in slightly lower yields than AAV9 at ~2.0 × 1013 vgs (Figure 1B). However, the reduction in packaging efficiency was more pronounced in the AAV9-DM, which yielded 4.5 × 1012 vgs (Figure 1B).

entries.proposition: The liver result, which is the paper's strongest and best-supported claim.
entries.snippet: AAV9-DM resulted in a ~127 fold reduction in vector genome copies as compared to AAV9, which is the most significant reduction in any variant tested (Figure 4A).
entries.anchor: Results, '3.4. Evaluation of Vector Genome Biodistribution in Different Tissues'

entries.proposition: THE CNS CLAIM IS WEAKER THAN THE SUMMARY STATES, BY THE PAPER'S OWN DATA: every mutant, including the new one, put significantly fewer vector genomes into the brain than the parent capsid.
entries.snippet: In the brain, all mutated capsids resulted in significantly lower vector genome copies as compared to AAV9, though relative expression levels were consistent amongst all capsids investigated.

entries.proposition: The summary sentence that the brain data above has to be read against.
entries.snippet: we have developed a new AAV9-DM capsid that possesses reduced liver tropism and reduced heart tropism, while minimally affecting CNS tropism as compared to AAV9

entries.proposition: The expression equivalence in CNS rests on a per-tissue relative ratio, and the whole-animal output fell by about two orders of magnitude.
entries.snippet: AAV9 was placed in the high group and reached a peak AR of 7.3 × 107, AAV9-16 and AAV9-HR were in the medium group and reached a peak AR of 6.6 × 106 and 3.5 × 106, respectively, and AAV9-DM was in the low group and reached a peak AR of 5.8 × 105 (Figure 2).
entries.anchor: Results, '3.3. AAV9-DM Capsid Results in Liver De-Targeting and Durable Transgene Expression'

entries.proposition: Vector genome copies and transgene expression disagreed in three of five tissues, and the authors propose the capsid itself modulates transcription — so neither read-out alone predicts the other.
entries.snippet: While the gene expression ratios are largely in line with vector genome copy data, some discrepancies occurred. In particular, AAV9-HR had higher relative gene expression ratios in the heart and GA from reduced genome copies.
entries.anchor: Results, '3.5. Evaluation of Fluc Relative Gene Expression Levels in Extrahepatic Tissues'

entries.proposition: The paper's own statement of why the dose ceiling is the problem worth solving, with the clinical deaths it cites.
entries.snippet: We believe that for AAV therapies to continue to move forward, the trend of administering high-vector doses must be abandoned in favor of developing efficient AAV vectors that are effective at lower, safer doses.

entries.proposition: The whole experiment is a single dose by one systemic route in one mouse strain with a luciferase reporter — which is the transfer limit on everything above.
entries.snippet: 1 × 1011 vgs/animal of AAV9, AAV9-16, AAV9-HR, or AAV9-DM capsids containing a Fluc transgene were injected into C57BL6/J mice via the tail vein.
entries.anchor: Results, '3.3. AAV9-DM Capsid Results in Liver De-Targeting and Durable Transgene Expression'

entries.proposition: Transgene expression from the new capsid was not stable over the nine weeks observed, declining significantly from the week-3 reference.
entries.snippet: the AAV9-DM mutant resulted in significantly reduced transgene expression levels at 6 and 9 weeks as compared to week 3, though no differences were seen at other timepoints (Figure 3B)
entries.anchor: Results, '3.3. AAV9-DM Capsid Results in Liver De-Targeting and Durable Transgene Expression'

entries.proposition: The precedent capsid the design builds on is reported to keep CNS transduction — a prior claim, not a measurement made here.
entries.snippet: Importantly, AAV9-HR results in CNS transduction and expression rates similar to what is achieved by AAV9 [20].
